propositions: A check whose pass result is indistinguishable from the producer never running cannot be distinguished from its own failure and must assert producer liveness before trusting any absence-derived verdict.

Nine documented instances split between two populations: five in shipped code (gate scripts, pgrep patterns, silent lookup misses) and four in test code (subprocess absence assertions, grep oracles over colorized output, harness convergence twins).

The fail-open pattern has a mirror: a check producing a confident failing result for a reason other than the condition (e.g. wrong input to git show) is equally unreliable and costs investigation in the opposite direction.

Fail-open language must be added to the existing tests criterion (test-oracle antipattern: absence assertions on subprocess/file/network output without liveness check) and the existing error-handling criterion (shipped-code triggers: silent lookup miss, unchecked returncode, pgrep self-match, invisible best-effort failure).

Calibration replay confirmed 9/9 pre-fix cases fire with attributed fail-open defects and 9/9 post-fix cases remain silent; no new criterion is needed — the language fires reliably from both host criteria.
Documentation via rebar explain review (code-review author guide) with two worked examples (instances 1 and 6) satisfies the AC without new infrastructure.
